newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Britain agree to allow prisoner transfers.
newsitem.headline: India, Britain agree to allow prisoner transfers.

text.p: India and Britain agreed on Monday to allow the transfer of prisoners between the two nations to enable offenders to serve time in their home countries.

British High Commissioner David Gore-Booth and Indian Additional Foreign Secretary R.S. Kalha initialled the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Agreement in the Indian capital, the British High Commission said.
The high commission said the agreement was the first step towards allowing Indian convicts in Britain and British offenders in India to serve their sentences in their respective countries.
"Both governments have now indicated their intent to make this a reality," it said in a statement.
The transfer authority is already covered in Britain by the Transfer of Prisoners Act of 1984. India's parliament will have to adopt enabling legislation.
Officials could not be reached to say how many prisoners from the two countries could be involved.
